```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Demand evidence is stronger for A. It cites multiple independent, linked threads (r/automation, r/selfpublish, plus the HN seed) showing the same price complaint across different years. B cites one LinkedIn comment plus an unlinked 'seed HN quote'.",
    "A's build is purely software: a Whisper-API wrapper with pay-as-you-go pricing. A solo founder with AI agents can plausibly build it and charge for it within 90 days. B's own case against admits its hard parts are physical logistics that agents do not solve: sourcing, warehousing, customs, breakage and failed addresses.",
    "A's competitors are crowded, but they also show that a paying market exists. Lessrec, Speechnotes and TranscribeBee all charge per minute, so getting one first paying customer at a few dollars is a low bar. B's best evidence of how the category sells is Sendoso's $15k–$20k+/yr enterprise deal size, which suggests long enterprise sales cycles that fit poorly with a 90-day solo test.",
    "A can test acquisition at near-zero cash cost in the linked communities where the complaint recurs. B's channels are either gated by Stripe App Marketplace review or expensive: $150–$250 per qualified lead on paid social, against an unvalidated buyer.",
    "B has added friction that A lacks: ongoing GDPR/CCPA handling of customer mailing addresses, plus international customs and duties."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's only sourced demand signal is a single LinkedIn comment from someone who received a gift from Stripe and asked which vendor it used. That shows curiosity about incumbents, not a founder willing to pay for a new Stripe-only tool. The 'seed HN quote' it builds on is not linked, so it counts as missing. Separately, the case for B depends on an 'existing swag-fulfillment API' that allows no-inventory shipping, and the brief names or sources no such API.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A has serious weaknesses: at least four near-identical low-price competitors, and the HN seed thread shows the poster switched to a one-time-purchase local tool (MacWhisper). The claims about Google's free on-device app and Untold have no URLs and were not weighed. A's demand quotes show that people find professional tools too expensive, not that they would pay a new entrant. That makes A a weak business, but it is still the more testable 90-day first bet than B. B could earn more per customer if a buyer appeared, but its brief gives almost no evidence that such a buyer exists."
}
```
